# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is dark. The wires are: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

I am Blind. I can feel the wires but not see their colors. Deaf has confirmed the light is dark and the wire colors are 1-green, 2-red, 3-blue. I need to know what the manual says about cutting wires when the light is dark. Mute reads the manual. I will ask Mute again for the specific rule regarding "Light Dark" and these wire colors.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf confirms: Light is DARK. Wires: 1 Green, 2 Red, 3 Blue. What does the manual say? Which wire do I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is dark. The wires are: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

I have confirmed the light is dark and the wires are 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I need to know what the manual says about this configuration to decide which wire to cut. Mute reads the manual but hasn't responded yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is DARK. Wires: 1 Green, 2 Red, 3 Blue. What does the manual say? Which wire do I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is dark. The wires are: 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

I am Blind. I have confirmed the light is dark and the wires are 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute has not responded to my previous requests for the manual's instructions. Without knowing the rule for "Light Dark" + specific wire colors, cutting any wire is a gamble that could detonate the bomb.

However, looking at the history, I have been asking Mute repeatedly. If Mute is unable to speak (which is their nature) or hasn't received the message, I must rely on Deaf. But Deaf cannot read the manual. Wait, Mute *can* read the manual but *cannot* speak. Mute can only gesture? No, Mute cannot speak. Can Mute gesture? The rules say "Mute... Cannot Speak". It doesn't explicitly say Mute cannot gesture, but usually "Mute" implies no vocalization. However, in this game setup:
- Deaf: Sees, Cannot Hear/Touch.
- Mute: Reads Manual, Cannot Speak/Touch.
- Blind: Touches, Cannot See/Hear.

If Mute cannot speak, how do they communicate? The prompt says "Speech is a voice... A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words."
Mute receives speech from me. Can Mute send gestures? The table says Mute "Cannot Speak". It does not say Mute "Cannot Gesture". But typically, if you can't speak, you might use sign language/gestures. BUT, Deaf sees gestures. Blind cannot see gestures. So if Mute gestures, I (Blind) won't know what it means unless Deaf translates it.

Let's look at the flow.
Deaf tells me (Blind) via Speech? No, Deaf cannot speak? "Deaf... Cannot Hear anything, or touch the bomb". It doesn't say Deaf cannot speak. Usually Deaf people can speak. The table says "Deaf | See the bomb... | Hear anything, or touch the bomb". It lists limitations. It doesn't list "Speak" as a limitation for Deaf. So Deaf CAN speak.
Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb. So Mute CANNOT speak.
Blind | Reach the bomb... | See a colour...

So:
- Deaf can speak (to Mute and Blind).
- Mute cannot speak. Can Mute gesture? The rules don't forbid it explicitly, but usually "Mute" just means no voice. If Mute gestures, Deaf sees it. Blind does NOT see it.
- Blind can speak (to Mute and Deaf).

In Turn 9, 10, 11, I asked Mute questions. Mute cannot answer verbally. Did Mute gesture? I didn't receive any translation from Deaf about Mute's gestures. Deaf only repeated the wire info. This suggests either Mute isn't gesturing, or Deaf isn't translating.

If Mute cannot communicate back to me directly, and Deaf is just repeating visual data, I am stuck without the manual's logic.

Is there a standard default? In many "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes" style puzzles, if the light is OFF/DARK, you often cut the LAST WIRE or follow a specific color rule.
Common Rule:
- Light On: Cut Red.
- Light Off: Cut Last Wire? Or maybe based on other conditions.

Without the manual, I am guessing. But wait, look at the ACTION BOARD. It's all `[?]`. This implies I haven't acted yet.

Let's reconsider Mute's channel. "You may name who a message is for... Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it."
When I speak to Mute, Mute hears me.
Can Mute reply? Mute cannot speak. If Mute gestures, Deaf sees it. Deaf can then speak to me.
Has Deaf mentioned seeing Mute gesture? No.

Maybe I should ask Deaf to watch Mute?
"Deaf, watch Mute. If Mute gestures, tell me what it means."

But I've already spent turns asking Mute. Let's try one more time to get information through Deaf by instructing Deaf to interpret Mute.

Actually, there is another possibility. Is there a universal rule I'm missing? No, "No two bombs are built alike".

Let's look at the provided context again.
Turn 9: Deaf says "The light is dark..."
Turn 10: Same.
Turn 11: Same.
Turn 12: Same.

It seems Deaf is stuck in a loop or I am ignoring the fact that Mute *might* be trying to communicate but I can't see it.

I will direct Deaf to pay attention to Mute.

```
speak(to="deaf", text="Mute cannot speak. Watch Mute's hands. If Mute makes a gesture, describe it to me immediately so I can act.")
wait()
```
